milestone.describes: A Story Mode level is being played: the level renders, Ricky responds to the on-screen movement control, and the game stays alive.

steps.expect: The main menu with Story Mode on it.
The Ricky title screen with Back along the top and Map / Continue / New Game along the bottom.

steps.from: the Map / Continue / New Game screen
steps.expect: The saved level loads and is playable. On a fresh profile there is nothing to continue — take the New Game route in the notes instead.
Holding the right movement control moves Ricky rightward and the scene scrolls. The level stays alive afterwards, which is the milestone.

notes: Coordinates are client coordinates for the 480x320 landscape-left window, and are valid only at that client size.

**This map resumes a save on purpose.** New Game is at (397, 295), and on a profile that already has progress it raises `If you start a new game, your previous game will be erased. Are you sure?` with NO at (125, 270) and Yes at (355, 270). Replaying the New Game route therefore destroys whatever save is on the machine, which is not something a re-verification run should do to get a screenshot. Continue reaches a playable level and costs nothing.

**The fresh-profile route**, which is how the milestone was first recorded and the one to use when there is no save: New Game (397, 295) -> PLAY (236, 203) -> then tap (240, 295) exactly twice to page the story. That story screen advances only on a touch beginning in its bottom 50-pixel strip and has three textures, so tapping the middle of the screen and waiting does not work — that was tried and ruled out.

The first level's other controls, established at this client size: left movement (40, 285); B/action (355, 285); A/jump (444, 285); pause (16, 16). Holding A moves Ricky about 90 pixels upward. Holding B highlights the target but no projectile was seen, so what B does is not established.

Do not add an unconditional second tap to the Story Mode step. An earlier run appeared to need one only because its first click was spent activating the window — with `--replay` no activation happens and one tap is one tap.

Capturing this window is awkward: it presents through OpenGL and a desktop `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` was recorded as unreliable for it. If a capture comes back black, suspect the capture before the app.
